lessons: Requisition review found that production drain/serve build Registry and CliClient in squatch/stages.py compose, which merge.py compose_pipeline reaches. Neither file is in the fixed ownership hooks, and the ticket pins the fence to exactly owns+hooks.

The live Timers instance is local to restart_session, composed by daemon.py compose_daemon_restart. restart.py and daemon.py are unfenced, so a journaled cooldown Timer has no sanctioned seam to reach the provider client.

Serve.compose builds its own Registry plus rework/triage CliClients, and __main__._triage_pass builds another. The ownership contract does not say which construction sites share one registry/cooldown payload.

Fixing this needs a plan edit to section 20's provider-cooldown-failover ownership. Add stages.py and merge.py (and restart/daemon, or journal-fold re-derivation) as measured on-demand hooks, name every client construction site, then regenerate.

Keep the approved parts: registry suffix, edges, tiers, budgets, the DATA_MARKER wording and the measured headroom assertions. Update tests/test_seeded_phase4_02.py OWNERSHIP and ON_DEMAND tables to match the revised contract.
reason: The fixed ownership contract omits the production composition owners (stages/merge, Timers lifetime seam) that requisition review requires, so the ticket as written cannot pass.
